reviewer: read-only pre-build code check and red team (validation-layer stand-in); no cargo, no build, no test
verdict_reason: Four small fixes in the two tested crates. Builder focused logs show the crates compile and 16/16 pass at the working tree, so nothing here breaks the build. But F1 makes the quiet receipt state something false on the Operator's machine, and a test pins that false value. F2 gives the wrong typed result on the one failure path the state machine exists to bound. Fixing after the bundled run would cost a second run.

findings.what: The quiet window loses WS_EX_NOACTIVATE and WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW as soon as it is shown, and the receipt still says both are set. make_quiet sets the style bits on the hidden window (202). quiet_style reads them back at 204. Then window.set_visible(true) at 208 goes through winit 0.30.13 WindowState::set_window_flags -> WindowFlags::apply_diff. Because the VISIBLE diff is non-empty, apply_diff calls SetWindowLongW(GWL_EXSTYLE, to_window_styles()) at registry winit-0.30.13/src/platform_impl/windows/window_state.rs:398-407. That value is WS_EX_WINDOWEDGE | WS_EX_ACCEPTFILES | WS_EX_APPWINDOW (ON_TASKBAR is set when there is no owner, window.rs:1339). For the whole run the window can be activated, is listed in Alt-Tab and carries WS_EX_APPWINDOW. The receipt's no_activate_style and tool_window_style come from the read taken before the show, and host_vulkan.rs:62 asserts that stale value. focus_changes 0 still holds on the scripted paths (winit's first show is SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE because MARKER_ACTIVATE is false, size changes use SWP_NOACTIVATE, minimise is SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE, restore is SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE), but nothing guarantees it any more. A stray click or activation would no longer be blocked.
findings.scenario: Any `window --quiet` run: the receipt at Handshake_Artifacts/WP-KERNEL-STUDIO/smb-vk-host-1/first-capture-painted-window.json says no_activate_style true, but GetWindowLongPtrW(GWL_EXSTYLE) after the show has no WS_EX_NOACTIVATE.
findings.fix: Call win32::make_quiet(handles.hwnd)? again right after window.set_visible(true). Take quiet_style at the end of the run (in release(), before the window drops) so receipt and test report the live style. Later winit calls in this run (request_inner_size and WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGED -> set_window_flags(MAXIMIZED false)) have an empty diff and return early, so the second call sticks.

findings.what: The surface-loss bound stops working as soon as a re-created surface is lost again. (SurfaceLost, SurfaceRecreated) moves to Stale, and from Stale another SurfaceLost restarts at SurfaceLost{attempts: 1}, so the attempt count never passes 1. This is the case SDL and DXVK hit: vkCreateWin32SurfaceKHR succeeds, but get_physical_device_surface_capabilities or create_swapchain then returns VK_ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR. settle cycles recreate_surface -> recreate -> SurfaceLost for 8 rounds, returns Skipped("recreated"), and the next tick repeats. The run never reports surface_unrecoverable (exit 3). It burns a device wait-idle plus a surface destroy and create every frame until the deadline, then exits 6 as a timeout. tests/machine.rs:37 feeds SurfaceLost repeatedly without SurfaceRecreated in between, so it misses this cycle.
findings.scenario: Feed Created, then repeat [SurfaceLost, SurfaceRecreated] 4 times, then SurfaceLost: the state ends at SurfaceLost{attempts:1}, not SurfaceUnrecoverable.
findings.fix: Keep the count across recovery. Add a `surface_attempts: u8` to Machine (or carry it in Stale) and reset it only on Signal::Presented. SurfaceLost from any state increments it, and above MAX_SURFACE_ATTEMPTS gives SurfaceUnrecoverable. Add that 4-cycle case to tests/machine.rs.

findings.what: After a failed swapchain re-create, the next attempt passes an already-retired swapchain as oldSwapchain, which the spec forbids. The spec retires oldSwapchain even when vkCreateSwapchainKHR fails. On ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR (265) recreate returns Ok and keeps self.swapchain = old. The next frame calls recreate again with that retired handle as old_swapchain (242), which VUID-VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR-oldSwapchain-01933 forbids. With no validation layer here, nothing would report it.
findings.scenario: A resize or DPI move lands between the capabilities query and create_swapchain, for example during the exercise or a WM_DPICHANGED.
findings.fix: In the OUT_OF_DATE arm, call self.destroy_swapchain() before returning Ok(()). The device is already idle from wait_idle at the top of recreate. The next create then runs with oldSwapchain null.

findings.what: After a fence timeout the command buffer is still pending, and the next submit resets it anyway. On TIMEOUT, submit_wait returns FenceTimeout but leaves the command buffer pending and the fence unsignalled-in-flight. The next Owner call (clear_pane, upload_pane or read_pane through the public GpuClientPort) runs begin(), which calls reset_command_buffer on a pending buffer (VUID-vkResetCommandBuffer-commandBuffer-00045) and then submits with a fence still in use. In Presenter::frame, any Err after a successful acquire leaves acquire_sem signalled, so the next acquire violates the unsignalled-semaphore rule. The native host treats every Err as terminal, so the host itself does not reach this. The public owner API does.
findings.scenario: A client gets FenceTimeout from upload_pane and retries.
findings.fix: Add a `poisoned: bool` to Submitter, set it on any submit_wait error, and have begin() return the stored refusal (FenceTimeout or DeviceLost) while it is set. Have Presenter::frame return the same refusal for every later call after an Err following acquire.

answers_to_lead.synchronization: Sound for a single queue with synchronous fence waits. Pane writes: UNDEFINED or TRANSFER_SRC -> TRANSFER_DST -> TRANSFER_SRC, all TRANSFER stages; a later submit reads after that barrier in submission order. Swapchain path: acquire semaphore waited at TRANSFER, matching the src stage of the UNDEFINED -> TRANSFER_DST barrier, then clear+barrier when the pane is smaller, blit, optional TRANSFER_SRC copy with a host-read barrier, then PRESENT_SRC at BOTTOM_OF_PIPE. Present semaphores are indexed by swapchain image. Fence waits are bounded at 5 s and acquire at 2 s, and the fence is reset after every successful wait. The command buffer is reused only after its fence, except the timeout path (F4). device_wait_idle in the Drop impls and the re-create paths is unbounded (bounded in practice by the Windows TDR turning a hang into DEVICE_LOST).
answers_to_lead.object_lifetime: Destruction order holds: Presenter (holds Arc<Core>) drops before Owner in window.rs release(); Core destroys device and instance last and clears OWNER_LIVE. Re-create destroys the old swapchain, its semaphores and the capture buffer only after the new swapchain exists; no image views are created, so swapchain images do not leak. Device lost leaves a terminal state; Drop destroys everything after a failing wait-idle (allowed after loss). Retired-handle reuse is F3. Rebind is not built (README says so).
answers_to_lead.spec_misuse: Checked: B8G8R8A8_UNORM + SRGB_NONLINEAR is selected from the surface's formats; BLIT_DST on optimal tiling is checked; R8G8B8A8_UNORM BLIT_SRC is a mandatory format feature. TRANSFER_SRC|DST are checked against supported_usage_flags (COLOR_ATTACHMENT is always supported). One queue family, EXCLUSIVE, QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED, so there is no ownership transfer. The presenting family is checked twice (vkGetPhysicalDeviceWin32PresentationSupportKHR at device pick and vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceSupportKHR in Presenter::new). current_extent is re-read on every re-create, so a DPI change becomes Resized -> Stale -> re-create at the new extent; 0 or u32::MAX means Minimized, with no acquire and no create; extents above 16384 are refused. Not a defect: after recreate_surface, SurfaceSupport is not re-queried for the new surface (VUID-VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR-surface-01270 asks for it), and the present-wait semaphores are destroyed after wait-idle without swapchain_maintenance1. The field does the same.
answers_to_lead.unsafe: native-host: crate-level #![deny(unsafe_code)] in lib.rs; win32.rs alone has a module-level #![allow(unsafe_code)]; each block is a read-only query or a style or show call on a window owned by this process, checked through owned(). window.rs has no unsafe. hsk-studio-vulkan: only #![deny(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]; it is the designated unsafe leaf; machine.rs and refusal.rs hold no unsafe; every block has a SAFETY comment and I found none wrong except the set_var justification ('before worker threads'), which is false under the test harness but harmless on Windows (process-local SetEnvironmentVariable plus the std env lock). HostBuffer's raw pointer makes Presenter !Send, so a Presenter cannot leave its creating thread; queue access needs a borrow of Owner, so borrowck rules out concurrent submits.
answers_to_lead.quiet: focus_changes is measured, not assumed: winit Focused(true) events plus a GetForegroundWindow poll once per about_to_wait. Only 5 samples per run per the receipts, and there is no EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND hook (the engineer's position asked for one). Every activation path I traced is no-activate (see F1). The quiet style itself is wiped at show: F1.
answers_to_lead.document_feature_closure: Default builds are clean. hsk-studio-vulkan depends only on ash (loaded, std, so libloading). native-host by default: vulkan, accord (no deps), observe (accord only), winit =0.30.13 with default-features=false and rwh_06, windows-sys, png, sha2. That closure has no egui, eframe or wgpu. Feature `document` enables harness-view `viewer`, which brings egui and render-gpu (wgpu), and `asset-local-test-host`, which brings harness-core. eframe comes only with harness-view `desktop`, so native-host Cargo.toml's comment 'links egui, eframe and wgpu' overstates; that is a doc nit, not a defect. No default-feature (non-document) check of native-host appears in the builder logs (every check and nextest run used --features document); the cfg(not(feature="document")) path read clean by eye.

There is no new [[package]]; png 0.18.1 and sha2 0.10.9 were already in the base lock, and the hsk-studio-vulkan entry (ash) is unchanged. answers_to_lead.demo_handshake: A true refusal, not a harness-view defect. In demo.handshake's document.json, working_space_rgb and blending_space are null, artboards is [], the only raster layer is visible:false, and its tile has format 'caller-selected-format' with a placeholder artifact handle. It is the session/harness-core edit fixture (revision 9) used by harness_drive, harness_headless and action_batch, not a renderable document. view_snapshot (render.rs:389-391) refuses no_working_profile on the Gpu and Cpu paths alike, so the egui harness would refuse it too. A candidate, if wanted, is a renderable demo fixture (assigned profile, an artboard, a visible layer with real tiles), not a viewer change. The brief's 'demo.handshake shows in the window' cannot be met with this file.
